subject: Russia
note: Hand-curated research for a Geographica episode about Lake Baikal. Claims are cited to a pinned Wikipedia revision (trusted_secondary). The lake has no outline in the pinned map data, so it is a labelled approximate point in southern Siberia. Russia is a flagged country (Crimea, Kuril Islands; none shown), so the episode needs the borders review before release. Belgium is outlined for scale, because the article compares the lake’s area to Belgium.

claims.text: Lake Baikal is a rift lake and the deepest lake in the world, with a maximum depth of 1,642 metres.
It is the world’s largest freshwater lake by volume, containing 22–23% of the world’s fresh surface water.
At 31,722 km², slightly larger than Belgium, it is the world’s seventh-largest lake by surface area.
It is 636 km long and 79 km wide.
It is situated in southern Siberia, Russia, between Irkutsk Oblast to the northwest and the Republic of Buryatia to the southeast.
It lies in a rift valley, created by the Baikal Rift Zone, where the Earth’s crust is slowly pulling apart.
